subject: Compaction canary guardrails + rollback (who can flip kill-switch?)
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM -0800
Subject: Compaction canary guardrails + rollback (who can flip kill-switch?)
Attachments: kv-compaction-canary-guardrails-v3.docx, runtime-1.22-rollout-rollback-matrix.xlsx

Team,

Ahead of the runtime-1.22 canary expansion, we need to lock:
1) guardrails (alert thresholds + time windows)
2) rollback criteria (auto vs manual)
3) authority: who can flip the compaction kill-switch during an incident

I attached v3 of guardrails + a draft rollback matrix. Please comment/approve today so we can wire this into the rollout controller.

Proposed guardrails for Hosted (canary cohort: us-west-2, 1% traffic, then 5%):
- Auto-rollback trigger A (tail): p99 end-to-end latency for /chat.completions > baseline*1.20 for 10 min AND compaction_enabled=true.
- Auto-rollback trigger B (errors): 5xx rate > 0.30% for 5 min OR request_shed > 0.10% for 5 min.
- Manual rollback trigger C (allocator): kv_evictions_total jump > 5x vs control AND customer-impacting latency page.
- Manual rollback trigger D (compaction pressure): compaction_bytes_moved_per_s > 2.0 GiB/s for 10 min OR compaction_time_ms p95 > 8ms (scheduler phase) for 10 min.

Kill-switch authority proposal:
- SRE on-call (IC) can flip kill-switch immediately when customer impact is suspected; no pre-approval required.
- Must page Runtime TL (Omar) and Runtime exec sponsor (Mateo) within 10 minutes.
- Re-enable only after joint SRE + Runtime TL sign-off.

Two questions we need answered:
- Are the thresholds too aggressive given mixed-length bursts? (We saw a short-lived spike in canary last week; don’t want flapping.)
- Do we want auto-rollback on “compaction pressure” signals (bytes moved / compaction time) alone, or only when coupled with tail/error regressions?

Thanks,
Sean
—
Sean Gallagher
Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 9:38 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Compaction canary guardrails + rollback (who can flip kill-switch?)

Agree on IC authority to flip immediately. If we’re wrong, we can sort it out later; if we’re right, we just saved an incident.

On thresholds: baseline*1.20 for p99 seems OK for 1% canary, but I’d strongly prefer to couple any auto action to customer-visible tail/error, not compaction internals.

i.e.
- bytes moved / compaction time should page and annotate, but not auto-rollback unless tail/error also breaches.

Omar: can you sanity check the compaction_time_ms p95 > 8ms number? Want to make sure it’s not inside expected variance when fragmentation is high.

Mateo



From: Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 10:07 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Compaction canary guardrails + rollback (who can flip kill-switch?)

Sanity check:
- For the scheduler-budgeted compaction step, on A100 we’re usually ~1–3ms p95 when it’s doing relocations, and near 0ms when idle.
- We saw ~6–7ms p95 in a synthetic fragmentation workload (benchmark-lab generator) at very high churn.

So p95 > 8ms sustained for 10min is a good “something’s off” signal, but I agree with Mateo: page + annotate, but don’t auto-rollback on it in isolation.

Also: compaction_bytes_moved_per_s > 2 GiB/s seems high enough that we’re probably chewing into decode time, but again it’s model/sequence-length dependent.

One request: if we do manual rollback trigger on “allocator/eviction anomaly”, please include pinned sessions as an exception (Dedicated has more of those). For Hosted canary, tier-aware eviction should mostly hit preemptible prefixes, but I don’t want the metric to panic us without tail impact.

-Omar



From: Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 11:26 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Compaction canary guardrails + rollback (who can flip kill-switch?)

+1 to separating:
- SLO guardrails (tail/error) => auto rollback
- “allocator health” (fragmentation, bytes moved, evictions) => paging + dashboards + investigation

If we bake this into standards, I’d like the auto-rollback conditions to be expressed in the rollout controller as:

AUTO_ROLLBACK = (p99_multiplier > 1.20 for 10m) OR (5xx > 0.30% for 5m) OR (shed > 0.10% for 5m)

And then require compaction_enabled=true as a tag/annotation, not a gating condition (otherwise we miss “compaction indirectly caused” cases where the flag toggled mid-window).

Re: “baseline” definition: can we define it as the control cohort in the same region + same model family (e.g., llama-3.*) rather than a static number? That will reduce seasonal/diurnal noise.

Allison



From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 12:04 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Compaction canary guardrails + rollback (who can flip kill-switch?)

On implementation in rollout policy engine:
- We can do cohort comparison for p99 and for 5xx (control vs canary), same region, same route.
- For shed, we only have absolute rate right now (no cohort tag), but we can approximate using canary pool metrics.

Proposal for “baseline*1.20” => p99_canary / p99_control > 1.20.

Kill-switch authority:
- Works with existing “emergencyDisable” path from PR-19422.
- We need a single source of truth for “who can flip”: I’ll add an entry in the oncall runbook plus a short note in the release checklist.

One detail: config propagation is ~60–120 seconds to 95% of pods. So if IC flips, we should expect 1–2 minutes before the p99 starts to recover. That should be called out to avoid a second panic toggle.

Paula



From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Benji Okafor <benji.okafor@redwoodinference.com>, Omar El-Sayed <omar.elsayed@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 19, 2026 at 11:03 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Compaction canary guardrails + rollback (who can flip kill-switch?)

I incorporated the authority language into the oncall playbook draft. Suggested wording:

- “During an active customer-impacting incident (SEV2+), the Incident Commander (SRE on-call) is authorized to set runtime.kv_compaction.enabled=false for the impacted hosted canary pools without additional approval. Notify Runtime TL + SRE manager ASAP; re-enable requires explicit Runtime TL approval.”

Also adding a step-by-step “if you flip it” checklist:
1) Post in #incidents with timestamp + rationale
2) Confirm rollout controller paused for the cohort
3) Watch: p99 (route + model breakdown), shed rate, 5xx, compaction_bytes_moved, evictions
4) Wait 2 minutes for config propagation before deciding it didn’t work

Sean: if you’re good with this, I’ll finalize the runbook page and link it in ENG-4829.

Rafael
—
Rafael Mendes
Production On-Call Readiness
Redwood Inference
